content: Malabathrum, also referred to as Malobathrum or Malabar leaf, is the term historically used in classical and medieval texts to describe the leaves of the plant Cinnamomum tamala (sometimes identified as Cinnamomum tejpata). In ancient Greece and Rome, these leaves were utilized to produce a fragrant oil known as Oleum Malabathri, which was highly valued. The leaves are mentioned in the 1st-century Greek text Periplus Maris Erytraei as one of the significant exports of the Tamil kingdoms in southern India. In medieval texts, the term Malabathrum was also used to describe the dried leaves of various trees within the genus Cinnamomum, which were believed to possess medicinal properties. These leaves, commonly known as tejpat, tej pat, tejpatta, or tejpata in Hindi, and tamalpatra in Marathi, are widely used in Indian cuisine, particularly in the Mughal cuisine of North India. However, they are often mistakenly labeled as Indian bay leaves. True bay leaves, derived from the Bay Laurel tree of Mediterranean origin, belong to a different genus and differ significantly in both appearance and aroma. Bay leaves are shorter, light to medium green in color, and have a single prominent vein running along their length. In contrast, tejpat leaves are approximately twice as long and wider than bay leaves. True tejpat leaves impart a strong cassiaor cinnamon-like aroma to dishes, whereas bay leaves have a scent more reminiscent of pine and lemon. Indian grocery stores typically stock authentic tejpat leaves, though in regions where they are unavailable, some stores may only offer Turkish bay leaves. Additionally, the bark of the Cinnamomum tamala tree is sometimes used in cooking, though it is considered inferior to true cinnamon or cassia. The term Malabar refers to a region on the western coast of southern India, which constitutes the northern part of the modern-day state of Kerala. The word Mala or Malaya translates to mountain in Tamil, Malayalam, and Sanskrit. The name Malabathrum is thought to have been derived from the Sanskrit term tamālapattram (तमालपत्रम्), which literally means dark-tree leaves.
